# Now 2.13.61
- Clicking a lyric now moves there once, cleanly. After any control action the app re-reads the player three times over the following second and a half to confirm what happened, and those reads could still report the position from before the jump. The lyrics followed each reading, so a single click could move the highlight three times, each with its own animation. Clicking backwards was worst, and would do it even one line at a time. The app now trusts its own jump until the player genuinely catches up.

# Now 2.13.60
- Clicking a lyric while you have scrolled away is now as gentle as any other line change. Two things move on a click: the song jumps to the line, and the scrolling you had done is handed back. They travel in opposite directions and mostly cancel, but only one of them was animated, so a small visible nudge was drawn as though it were a huge leap. Both now move together on a single curve, sized by how far the words actually travel on screen.

# Now 2.13.59
- Line changes now spring by the same amount however far they travel. Previously the bounce was a proportion of the distance moved, so two long wrapped lines in a row lurched, and clicking a line far away threw the whole list around. A single line change is unchanged; everything longer now arrives composed, and takes slightly longer to cross the distance instead of whipping. - Scrolling the lyrics no longer blurs and dims the lines you are reading. Focus used to be measured from the line being sung, which is off screen once you scroll away, so the lines you had scrolled to were the faintest on screen. While you are scrolling everything stays sharp and legible, with the line being sung still marked so you can find your way back.
